classes.label: bencode
classes.summary: The one encoding under everything in BitTorrent: four value types, each self-delimiting, with a canonical form so that the same value has exactly one byte representation.

classes.label: BencodeType
classes.summary: The four value types of bencode.

classes.label: canonical form
classes.summary: What makes a bencoding canonical.

classes.label: metainfo
classes.summary: The .torrent file: a bencoded dictionary describing one file or one directory tree as a sequence of fixed-size pieces, each named by its SHA-1.

classes.label: MetaInfo
classes.summary: The top-level dictionary of a .torrent file.

classes.label: Info
classes.summary: The dictionary the infohash covers.

classes.label: FileEntry
classes.summary: One file of a multi-file torrent.

classes.label: metainfo validity
classes.summary: What a decoded MetaInfo must satisfy to describe a torrent at all.

classes.label: tracker
classes.summary: How a peer finds other peers for an infohash.

classes.label: URL query
classes.summary: Fields as key=value pairs in a URL's query string, each value percent-encoded; raw bytes (the infohash, the peer id) are percent-encoded byte by byte.

classes.label: binary
classes.summary: A fixed layout: the fields in order, each with a wireType (big-endian integers of a given width, fixed-size byte strings, or the rest of the message), nothing self-describing.

classes.label: AnnounceEvent
classes.summary: What an announce says about the peer's state.

classes.label: AnnounceRequest
classes.summary: What a peer tells an HTTP tracker, as the query string of a GET to the announce URL.

classes.label: AnnounceResponse
classes.summary: An HTTP tracker's answer: how often to come back, how many peers it knows, and some of them.

classes.label: Peer
classes.summary: A peer in dictionary form, as a tracker lists them when not compact.

classes.label: ScrapeResponse
classes.summary: The answer to GET <scrape URL>?info_hash=…: counts per infohash, without any peers.

classes.label: CompactPeer
classes.summary: Six bytes: an IPv4 address and a port, both big-endian.

classes.label: UdpConnectRequest
classes.summary: The first message to a UDP tracker: a fixed magic number proves the sender speaks the protocol; the tracker answers with a connection id to use for 60 seconds.

classes.label: UdpAnnounceRequest
classes.summary: The announce over UDP: the same facts as the HTTP query, in 98 fixed bytes.

classes.label: UdpAnnounceResponse
classes.summary: 20 bytes of header, then compact peers to the end of the datagram.

classes.label: tracker exchange
classes.summary: What a client checks on what a tracker sends back.

classes.label: Tracker
classes.summary: A tracker as an entry in a list of known trackers (data/trackers.jsonld): where it is, which protocol it speaks, who runs it as far as is known, and where the entry came from.

classes.label: KnownTorrent
classes.summary: A torrent whose infohash is known and named (data/torrents.jsonld), so that a tracker's counts for it can be shown under a name.

classes.label: wire
classes.summary: What two peers say to each other once connected: a 68-byte handshake naming the torrent, then length-prefixed messages — which pieces each has, who may ask whom, requests for 16 KiB blocks and the blocks themselves.

classes.label: Handshake
classes.summary: The first 68 bytes each way.

classes.label: ReservedBit
classes.summary: Flags in the handshake's reserved bytes: byte index from 0, bit value within the byte.

classes.label: MessageId
classes.summary: The byte after the length prefix.

classes.label: Frame
classes.summary: Every message after the handshake: a big-endian length, then that many bytes — the id and its payload.

classes.label: Extended
classes.summary: Message id 20: one more id byte, then the payload.

classes.label: ExtendedHandshake
classes.summary: Sent right after the handshake by both sides when both set the extension bit.

classes.label: UtMetadata
classes.summary: Extension 'ut_metadata': the info dictionary fetched in 16 KiB pieces from a peer, so a magnet link suffices.

classes.label: UtPex
classes.summary: Extension 'ut_pex': peers tell each other about peers, as compact lists of those added and dropped since the last message, with a flag byte per added peer.

classes.label: peer wire
classes.summary: What a peer checks on what the other sends.

classes.label: webseed
classes.summary: A plain HTTP server as a peer: a client that knows a URL of the content (from 'url-list' or a magnet's 'ws=') fetches blocks with Range requests and verifies the pieces exactly as if a peer had sent them.

classes.label: WebSeedRequest
classes.summary: What a block request becomes over HTTP: a GET of the right URL with a Range header.

classes.label: webtorrent
classes.summary: BitTorrent in a browser.

classes.label: JSON
classes.summary: One JSON object per WebSocket text message.

classes.label: SessionDescription
classes.summary: A WebRTC session description as the browser's RTCPeerConnection gives it: an offer or an answer with its SDP text, which carries the ICE candidates (addresses) once gathering is complete.

classes.label: WsOffer
classes.summary: One offer in an announce: a fresh WebRTC offer and a random 20-byte id for it, so the answer can be matched.

classes.label: WsAnnounce
classes.summary: The announce a browser sends, with offers for the peers it hopes to meet.

classes.label: WsAnnounceReply
classes.summary: The tracker's own reply to an announce: the counts and the interval.

classes.label: WsOfferForwarded
classes.summary: What a peer receives when the tracker forwards another peer's offer to it: the offer, its id, and the offerer's peer id.

classes.label: WsAnswer
classes.summary: An answer to a forwarded offer.

classes.label: nostr
classes.summary: Finding a torrent in the first place.

classes.label: Nostr event
classes.summary: A NIP-01 event: one JSON object with 'id', 'pubkey', 'created_at', 'kind', 'tags', 'content' and 'sig'.

classes.label: Nostr tags
classes.summary: A value held in an event's tags rather than in its JSON keys.

classes.label: TorrentKind
classes.summary: The two event kinds NIP-35 defines.

classes.label: ReferencePrefix
classes.summary: The prefixes an 'i' tag may carry, each naming an external database the content is listed in: ['i', 'imdb:tt15239678'].

classes.label: NostrEvent
classes.summary: The envelope every Nostr event shares (NIP-01).

classes.label: TorrentEvent
classes.summary: A torrent listing, kind 2003: the tags of a NostrEvent read as fields.

classes.label: FileTag
classes.summary: ['file', name, size]: one file of the torrent.

classes.label: TorrentComment
classes.summary: A reply to a listing, kind 2004, threaded exactly as a kind 1 note is (NIP-10): an 'e' tag naming the listing, a 'p' tag naming its author.

classes.label: torrent event validity
classes.summary: What a kind 2003 event must satisfy to be a listing at all, and — when the .torrent is also at hand — to be a listing of that torrent.
